correctness.rationale: For n>=1 the coefficient of e_(kn+ell) is a_ell n/(kn+ell) b_n/b_(kn+ell), converging uniformly over the finite set of ell to c a_ell with c=k^(-(alpha+3)/2). Hence C-c g(S)V_k is a finite sum of compact diagonal-weighted shifts. The k mutually orthogonal residue channels yield the exact Gram sum Σ g_r(S)^*g_r(S)=T_(Σ|g_r|²). Toeplitz Calkin symbol calculus gives the full positive interval and optimal essential norm. R(Cf)=g Rf(z^k) proves kernel=constants; Hardy boundary-kernel Weyl sequences and positive Fredholm Gram theory give the sharp closed-range equivalence. The polynomial divisibility test follows from a k-th-root Fourier filter; projected-output dimensions rule out Fredholmness. Finite-band Toeplitz trace moments plus finite-rank approximation of compacts prove the continuous-test-function finite-section bulk law. Full coefficient asymptotics and the Hardy endpoint were separately reconstructed. Finite script check.py passed 2368 supplementary assertions, but it cannot certify infinite statements.

originality.rationale: The combined statement is the precise positive Calkin Gram model, exhaustive full-boundary-orbit closed-range classification, and finite-section bulk law for noncompact polynomial power-map Volterra companions for all k>=2 and fixed alpha>=-1. Dong–Xu gives general geometric compactness/essential-norm estimates without the explicit algebraic three-part classification in the inspected definition/statement material. Singh et al. study ordinary slant operator spectra and compactness, not this Gram law. The known antipodal slant theorem *does* imply a closely related k=2 essential norm, so that restricted norm is explicitly not treated as novel. Classical Toeplitz/Szegő machinery also is not novel. An inaccessible directly relevant slant full text and a broader implicit weighted-composition reduction remain genuine risks; no exhaustive uniqueness claim is made.
residual_risks: The complete text of the directly relevant published antipodal slant result could not be inspected; its provided summary already covers the k=2 norm component.
A broad general weighted-composition or analytic slant singular-spectrum theorem may imply some or all of the combined classification despite lack of matching accessible formulations.
The motivating paper’s full proof/appendix could not be re-opened during the final comparison; accessible introduction and main statements were read.

value.rationale: The closed-range question for a natural family of noncompact Volterra companions is mathematically distinct from compactness and norm estimates. A single symbol with a boundary zero may have closed range if that zero fails to cover a full power-map fiber, while k-th-root orbit divisibility forces nonclosed range. The complete algebraic boundary criterion, continuous essential singular interval and explicit finite-section distribution give jointly useful stability and spectral approximation information for every polynomial symbol, power degree and fixed Hilbert weight. In the basic k=2 case g=1-z versus g=1-z² demonstrates a decisive qualitative distinction, beyond routine norm estimation. The result does not rely for value on novelty of classical Toeplitz or k=2 norm formulas.
